source: IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 — Registered Voters per County Assembly Ward (First Schedule); Kenya Data Atlas P23X ward-voter materialisation (scripts/p23/build-ward-voters.mjs, data/sprint2/README.md)
refresh_trigger: Replace this closure once the ten Mandera East/Lafey County Assembly Ward source rows can be deterministically and uniquely crosswalked to canonical 2012-01 ward geometry (by official code or an audited name match) without residual ambiguity, or once an authoritative reconciled boundary layer for this county is adopted; then materialise the governed observation for each ward using the same audited method already applied to the other 1,440 wards in scripts/p23/build-ward-voters.mjs.
reason: The Kenya Data Atlas already materialises registered-voter counts for 1,440 of the 1,450 statistical wards directly from IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 (scripts/p23/build-ward-voters.mjs). Ten official source rows across two constituencies remain withheld from canonical ward geometry: Mandera East (constituency 43 — Arabia, Bulla Mpya, Khalalio, Neboi, Township) and Lafey (constituency 44 — Libehia, Fino, Lafey, Warankara, Alungo Gof). The current externally sourced ward boundary layer for this pair of constituencies conflicts with the operative IEBC configuration, so a safe deterministic one-to-one crosswalk between the ten official CAW source rows and the ten canonical ward polygons cannot be established without risking a false attribution of a specific voter count to the wrong ward. This is the same documented Mandera East/Lafey spatial hold referenced throughout the Atlas (CHANGELOG.md; docs/DATA-COMPLETION-PLAN.md, Track B and the P24 acceptance criteria) and deliberately preserved through the P23A/P23X constituency and ward voter materialisation: the ten source rows remain correctly included in the Mandera East and Lafey constituency-level totals as an exact aggregation of all official First Schedule child-ward rows, but are not force-matched, interpolated, or evenly split across the five ward polygons in either constituency at the ward level. The ward-level completeness ledger slot for these ten wards is therefore closed as boundary unresolved — a genuine geometry/crosswalk constraint distinct from data non-publication — rather than left as an unexplained blank or filled with a fabricated or force-matched value.
